Title: Army Forge URL Source: https://army-forge.onepagerules.com/armyInfo/7el7k3hgy5pb9o9i/2/preview Markdown Content: [![Image 1: Home](https://army-forge.opr-cdn.com/app/onepagerules_round_128x128.png)](https://army-forge.onepagerules.com/) Machine Cults [Studio](https://army-forge.onepagerules.com/studio "Army Forge Studio") [Sign In](https://army-forge.onepagerules.com/auth/signin) GF - Machine Cults v3.5.3 ## Intro The Machine Cult are a faction of humans who have sought to enhance their bodies with machinery to become something greater. These enhancements have allowed them to become a highly specialized army with a great deal of mobility, giving them an edge in rough environments. These cults have embraced the inevitable transcendence of machines, and work to merge themselves with their machines, but this process has caused them to become isolated and outcast from the rest of humanity. Despite their faith and patience, the promise of transcendence still eludes them even after centuries of devotion. ## About OPR OPR (www.onepagerules.com) is the home of many free games which are designed to be fast to learn and easy to play. This project was made by gamers for gamers and it can only exist thanks to the support of our awesome community. If you want to help us in making more awesome content, you can support us on www.patreon.com/onepagerules Thank you for playing! ## Background Story The Machine Cult trace their origins to old Earth. Their cult has long believed that the advancement of technology is inevitable and eventually humanity itself will be surpassed by the machine in an event called the Singularity, which would have absolute power to determine the fate of humanity. The Cult believes that only by embracing the machine can humanity remain relevant, and their cult rejected the Founder and his plan for humanity, believing that his genetic enhancements were mere distractions from the inevitable machine Singularity. The Founder in turn banned their cult, and as a result, many Machine Cultists eagerly joined the refugee fleet. When humanity arrived in Sirius, the Machine Cult and its members were scattered throughout many of the surviving colonies. Though far apart, they were united in their faith and their fascination with augmentation. The Cult gained adherents from those who believed that their upgrades were the best way to adapt to new worlds. Driven on by discoveries in Sirius and trade with newly encountered species, the Machine Cult began to augment themselves in ways which could not have been imagined previously. As augmentation became more easily obtained, many of its adherents began to augment themselves beyond anything that they were capable of on Earth, seeking to embrace the machine in new ways. As they did so, the adherents of the cult began to grow apart from other colonists. Others began to see the Cult and their followers as strange and inhuman. Some even began to leave the cult, embittered by augmentation failures or haunted by a feeling that they had lost some part of humanity. As a result, the Machine Cult began to petition the Great Human Alliance for settlement rights. Their augmentations and robots allowed them to settle a number of inhospitable worlds which were otherwise not suited for settlements. The Machine Cult’s detachment and isolation meant that few were surprised when the Cult demanded independence from the Alliance. The Alliance were not interested in resettling or occupying the worlds the Cult had claimed and saw little to gain from war, and as such, the Machine Cults gained their final independence diplomatically, rather than through war. The Machine Cults still maintain their eternal vigil, awaiting the transcendence of technology and the ascension of the machine. Their forces search throughout the Sector, seeking hidden and lost technologies that might help this come about or allow them to more fully embrace the machine. 285pts | 2 GF - Machine Cults v3.5.3 ## Army-Wide Special Rule Machine-Fog:When units where all models have this rule are shot or charged from over 9" away, enemy units get -1 to hit rolls. ## Special Rules Bounding:When this unit is activated, you may place all models with this rule in it anywhere fully within D3+1" of their position. Crossing Attack:Once per activation, when this model moves through enemy units, pick one of them and roll X dice. For each 6+ the target takes one wound. Grounded Stealth:If a unit where all models have this rule has most of them within 1" of terrain, enemies get -1 to hit rolls when attacking them. Hit & Run Shooter:Once per round, units where all models have this rule may move by up to 3" after shooting. Lacerate:When attacking the target must re-roll unmodified Defense results of 6. Machine-Fog Boost:If all models in this unit have Machine-Fog, enemies attacking them always get -1 to hit rolls from Machine-Fog (instead of only when being shot/charged from over 9" away). Melee Shrouding:Enemies get -3" movement to a min. of 6" when trying to charge units where all models have this rule. Melee Slayer:When this model charges, its weapons get AP(+2) if most models in the target have Tough(3) or higher. Mend:Once per activation, before attacking, pick one friendly model within 3" with Tough, and remove D3 wounds from it. Piercing Debuff:Once per activation, before attacking, pick one enemy unit within 18" in line of sight, which loses AP(+1) when attacking once (next time the effect would apply). Screened:When units where all models have this rule are shot or charged from over 9" away, enemy units get -1 to hit rolls. Shred:On unmodified results of 1 to block hits, this weapon deals 1 extra wound. Strafing:Once per activation, when this model moves through enemy units, pick one of them and attack it with this weapon as if it was shooting. This weapon may only be used in this way. Surge:On unmodified results of 6 to hit, this weapon deals 1 extra hits (only the original hit counts as a 6 for special rules). Teleport:Once per activation, before attacking, you may place this model anywhere fully within 3" of its position when using Advance/Charge actions, or fully within 6" of its position when using Rush actions. Unpredictable:When attacking, roll one die and apply one effect to all models with this rule: on a 1-3 they get AP(+1), and on a 4-6 they get +1 to hit rolls instead. Unpredictable Fighter:When in melee, roll one die and apply one effect to all models with this rule: on a 1-3 they get AP(+1), and on a 4-6 they get +1 to hit rolls instead. Versatile Attack:When this unit is activated, pick one effect: until the end of the activation, when shooting or charging enemies over 9" away, all models with this rule in this unit either get AP(+1) or get +1 to hit rolls. ## Aura Special Rules Machine-Fog Boost Aura:This model and its unit get Machine-Fog Boost. Melee Shrouding Aura:This model and its unit get Melee Shrouding. Rending when Shooting Aura:This model and its unit get Rending when shooting. Teleport Aura:This model and its unit get Teleport. Unpredictable Fighter Aura:This model and its unit get Unpredictable Fighter. ## Army Spells **Cyborg Assault (1):** Pick one friendly unit within 12", which gets Hit & Run Shooter once (next time the effect would apply). **Power Beam (1):** Pick one enemy model within 18", which takes 2 hits with AP(1). This effect is resolved as if the target was a unit of [1]. **Shrouding Incense (2):** Pick up to two friendly units within 12", which get Machine-Fog Boost once (next time the effect would apply). **Searing Shrapnel (2):** Pick one enemy unit within 12", which takes 4 hits with AP(1) and Lacerate. **Corrode Weapons (3):** Pick up to three enemy units within 18", which loses AP(1) when shooting once (next time the effect would apply). **Crushing Force (3):** Pick one enemy unit within 12", which takes 6 hits with AP(2). 3 GF -
